packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.i: Forests whose rows carry item data. An item forest pairs a raw `Forest` (row ids and depths) with a way to look up the `StructureRow` for each row id. The package also holds the builder interfaces that generators use to emit rows, and a ready builder implementation.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.r: The raw forest model: an ordered list of row ids, each with a depth, which together encode a set of trees. Contains the `Forest` interface, its array-backed implementation `ArrayForest` with all editing operations, and the callback and control interfaces used to walk a forest top-down or bottom-up.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generato: The generator extension point. Generators are plugin modules (inserters, extenders, groupers, sorters, filters) that build or transform part of a forest automatically, and may optionally react to user edits of the generated rows. The package holds the service provider interfaces that generator authors implement, the context objects the plugin passes to them, the `GeneratorManager` service that stores generator instances, and constants naming built-in generators and common parameters.

Helpers for generator authors: abstract base classes with sensible defaults for each generator kind, ready-made item change filters and update checkers, an issue-only applicability checker, and a helper that loads attribute values for the rows a generator is working on while arranging re-generation when those values change.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.i18n: A minimal localisation abstraction: an `I18n` object resolves message keys to text in one locale, and an `I18nProvider` gives one for the current user. The Jira-backed implementations delegate to Jira's own i18n helper.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.i.summary: An `ItemForest` that holds its own copy of every `StructureRow` it contains, so it does not depend on any row service. Instances are created only through the static factory methods. The class is final and marked immutable; the row map is an unmodifiable copy. Caveat: the forest passed to `rearrangeItemForest`, `copySubtree` and `of(StructureRow)` is stored as given, not copied or frozen, so immutability of `getForest()` is only guaranteed for instances made by `of(Forest, Map)` and `copy`. Safe to share between threads when built from immutable inputs.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.r.summary: The standard `Forest` implementation, backed by a list of row ids and a parallel list of depths. It is mutable until `makeImmutable()` is called and provides editing operations (merge, move, remove, reorder, replace) that keep the forest invariants as long as inputs are valid. Row ids 0 and -1 are rejected; the other invariants are checked only when JVM assertions are enabled, and `getDiagnostics` can be used to validate explicitly. Clients create it with constructors; it is not thread-safe, and read methods return live views where noted.

Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if any row id is 0 or -1. Other invariants (equal sizes, depth rules, uniqueness) are only checked when JVM assertions are enabled; otherwise invalid input is accepted silently and later behaviour is undefined.

Same as `mergeForest(forest, under, after)` but any `StructureException` is swallowed silently, leaving the forest unchanged in that case. Note the argument order differs from `mergeForest`.

Inserts `forest` under row `under` (0 for the top level), right after the sibling `after` (0 to insert as the first child). If the two forests share no rows the whole forest is inserted in one step. Otherwise rows already present here are moved (with their existing subtrees) to the position they have in `forest`, and new rows are inserted; in each parent the merged children come first, in `forest` order, followed by children that were there before. Null or empty `forest` does nothing. `after` that is not found or is not a child of `under` (after resolving it to its ancestor at the target level) is ignored with an info log, giving first-child position. Throws `ForestMergeStructureException` if `under` or one of its ancestors occurs in `forest` (the merge would create a cycle), `StructureException` with code `INVALID_FOREST_OPERATION` if `under` is not in this forest, `UnsupportedOperationException` if immutable. The event handler, if not null, is told about every removal and insertion.
members.addRow(long, long, long): Places a single row under `under` after `after` (same position rules as `mergeForest`). If the row already exists it is moved there with its subtree; otherwise it is inserted as a leaf. Returns false (doing nothing) if `row` is 0, true otherwise. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` for row -1, `StructureException` if `under` is not found or is the row itself or one of its descendants, `UnsupportedOperationException` if immutable.
Inserts `forest` as is under `under` after `after`, without checking for rows that already exist here; the caller guarantees the forests share no rows (otherwise the result has duplicates and is invalid). Depths are shifted to fit below `under`. Null or empty forest does nothing. Throws `StructureException` if `under` is not found, `UnsupportedOperationException` if immutable. Invalid `after` is ignored as in `mergeForest`.

The handler, if not null, gets `beforeSubtreeRemoved` before the rows go.

Bottom-up fold. For each row, once all its children have been processed, calls `closure.visitRow(control, row, children, carry)` where `carry` is the accumulation of its children's results (null for leaves). Each result is then folded into its siblings' accumulation with `closure.combine(control, result, carry)`; siblings are combined from the last to the first. Returns the accumulation of the roots' results, or null if the forest is empty or the walk was cancelled through `control.cancel()`.
members.scanDownwards(com.almworks.jira.structur: Top-down scan: calls `scanner.acceptRow(control, row)` for each row in forest order. Through the `ForestScanControl` the scanner can read the position, skip the current subtree or the rest of an ancestor's subtree, or cancel the scan. Does nothing on an empty forest.
Walks the forest bottom-up and calls the visitor once for every row, after all of that row's descendants have been visited, passing the forest, the row id and the ids of its direct children (in order; empty for leaves). Rows are processed from the end of the forest towards the start. The visitor is not called for the invisible top level (the list of roots). If the visitor returns false the walk stops.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.r.summary: Read-only view of a forest: a sequence of row ids with a depth for each, in pre-order, that encodes an ordered set of trees. Invariants: row ids are unique and non-zero (and not -1, which is reserved for the super-root); the first row has depth 0; each depth is at most one more than the previous one. members.getPrecedingSiblingsForIndex(int): All earlier siblings of the row at `index`, in forest order (nearest last). Empty for index 0 or negative. Returns a new list.
members.getNextSiblingIndex(int): Index of the next sibling of the row at `index` (first later row at the same depth before any shallower row), or -1 if none or if `index` is negative or is the last index.
members.getNextSiblingForIndex(int): Row id of the next sibling of the row at `index`, or 0 if none.
members.getNextSibling(long): Row id of the next sibling of `row`, or 0 if none, not found, or `row` is 0.
members.getPathIndexAtDepth(int, int): Index of the ancestor of the row at `index` that sits at `depth` (the row itself if its depth equals `depth`). Returns -1 if `index` or `depth` is negative or if `depth` is greater than the row's depth.
members.getLastChild(long): Row id of the last direct child of `parent`; with `parent` 0, the last root. Returns 0 if the parent has no children or is not in the forest.
members.getLastChildByIndex(int): Row id of the last direct child of the row at `parentIndex`; a negative index means the last root. Returns 0 if there are no children or if `parentIndex` is not less than `size()`.
members.getChildrenIndicesIterator(int): Iterator over the indexes of the direct children of the row at `index`, in order. A negative index iterates over the roots. The iterator reads the forest lazily, so the forest must not change while it is used.
members.getChildren(long): Direct children of `row` in order; with `row` 0, the roots. Empty if the row is not found or has no children. Returns a new list.
members.getChildrenAtIndex(int): Direct children of the row at `index`, in order. Empty for a negative index. Returns a new list.
members.getRoots(): All rows of depth 0, in order. Returns a new list.
members.getPath(long): Path from the root down to `row`, inclusive (root first). Empty if the row is not found. Returns a new list.
members.getPathForIndex(int): Path from the root down to the row at `index`, inclusive. Empty for a negative index.
members.getParentPathForIndex(int): Path from the root down to the parent of the row at `index` (the row itself excluded). Empty for roots and for a negative index.
members.filter(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.u: Returns a forest containing only rows accepted by `filter`. A rejected row is dropped but its descendants are still tested; accepted descendants move up and take the place of the dropped row (they attach to the nearest accepted ancestor, or become roots). Order is preserved. A null filter, or one that accepts every row, returns this same instance rather than a copy; otherwise a new mutable forest is returned. The filter is called once per row at most.
members.filterSoft(com.almworks.jira.structure.a: Returns a forest with every row accepted by `filter` plus all ancestors of accepted rows, so the hierarchy of matching rows is preserved. Rejected rows with no accepted descendant are dropped. A null filter, or one accepting every row, returns this same instance; otherwise a new mutable forest.
members.filterHardest(com.almworks.jira.structur: Returns a forest from which every rejected row is removed together with its whole subtree; descendants of rejected rows are not tested. Depths of kept rows are unchanged. A null filter, or one accepting every row, returns this same instance; otherwise a new mutable forest.
members.subtree(long): New mutable forest with `row` as the single root followed by all its descendants, depths re-based so the row has depth 0. Empty forest if the row is not found.
members.subtreeAtIndex(int): Same as `subtree` for the row at `index`; empty forest for a negative index.
members.copySubforest(long): New mutable forest with the descendants of `row` (the row itself excluded), re-based so its children become roots. With `row` 0 returns a copy of the whole forest. Returns an empty forest if the row has no children and null if the row is not in the forest.
members.copySubforestAtIndex(int): Same as `copySubforest` for the row at index `k`: null for a negative index, empty for a leaf, otherwise the descendants with its children as roots.
members.copy(): Returns an independent mutable `ArrayForest` with the same rows and depths. The copy is not immutable even if this forest is.
Walks the forest bottom-up and calls the visitor once for every row, after all of that row's descendants have been visited, passing the forest, the row id and the ids of its direct children (in order; empty for leaves). Rows are processed from the end of the forest towards the start. The visitor is not called for the invisible top level (the list of roots). If the visitor returns false the walk stops.
Bottom-up fold. For each row, once all its children have been processed, calls `closure.visitRow(control, row, children, carry)` where `carry` is the accumulation of its children's results (null for leaves). Each result is then folded into its siblings' accumulation with `closure.combine(control, result, carry)`; siblings are combined from the last to the first. Returns the accumulation of the roots' results, or null if the forest is empty or the walk was cancelled through `control.cancel()`.
members.scanDownwards(com.almworks.jira.structur: Top-down scan: calls `scanner.acceptRow(control, row)` for each row in forest order. Through the `ForestScanControl` the scanner can read the position, skip the current subtree or the rest of an ancestor's subtree, or cancel the scan. Does nothing on an empty forest.
members.toFullString(): Text form listing every row as `row:depth`, without truncation. In `ArrayForest` the format is `forest(` then `ro,` if immutable, then comma-separated `row:depth` pairs, then `)`.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.r.summary: Optional listener passed to `ArrayForest` editing methods (merge, move, remove) to be told about each structural change, for example to keep side data in sync. Implemented by callers; the forest calls it synchronously during the operation. A move is reported as a removal followed by an insertion.

members.beforeSubtreeRemoved(com.almworks.jira.s: Called just before rows are removed. Arguments: the forest being changed, the start index (inclusive) and end index (exclusive) of the rows about to be removed, and a copy of the removed subtree re-based to depth 0.
members.afterForestInserted(com.almworks.jira.st: Called right after rows are inserted. Arguments: the forest being changed, the start index (inclusive) and end index (exclusive) of the inserted rows in it, and the inserted forest as passed in (with its own depths, before shifting).

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.r.summary: Position and control object handed to callbacks during a forest walk (`foldUpwards`, `scanDownwards`). members.getDepth(): Depth of the row currently being visited (0 for roots).

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.r.summary: Thrown by `ArrayForest.mergeForest` when the merge point (`under`) or one of its ancestors also appears in the forest being merged, so merging would make a row its own ancestor. members.<init>(long, long, com.almworks.jira.str: Creates the exception. Arguments: the merge point row, the row on the merge point's path that also occurs in the source forest, the source forest (being merged), and the target forest. The second row must be present in the source forest (otherwise an index error occurs while computing its root). The full text of both forests is captured only when trace logging is enabled for this class; otherwise placeholders are stored.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.r.summary: Callback for `Forest.foldUpwards`, a bottom-up fold where each row is visited after its children. Type `T` is the per-row result, `C` the accumulation of sibling results. Implemented by callers.

Folds one child's result into the accumulation for its siblings and returns the new accumulation. Arguments: the control (positioned at that child), the child's result, and the accumulation so far (null for the first call at a level). Siblings are combined from the last one to the first.
members.visitRow(com.almworks.jira.structure.api: Visits one row after all its children and returns its result (may be null). Arguments: the control (positioned at the row), the row id, the ids of its direct children in forest order (empty for leaves; the list is reused and valid only during the call), and the accumulation of the children's results (null for leaves). Call `control.cancel()` to abort the fold.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.r.summary: Convenience base for `ForestParentChildrenClosure` whose accumulation is simply a list of the children's results. Subclasses implement only `visitRow`. Not thread-safe; one instance per fold.

members.<init>(): Creates the closure with an empty internal pool of lists.
Adds `value` to the list for the current level and returns it, starting a fresh (cleared) list when `carry` is null. Because children are combined from last to first, the list holds the children's results in reverse forest order. The list objects are reused per depth, so a `visitRow` implementation must not keep a reference to the list it receives after it returns.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.r.summary: Callback for `Forest.visitParentChildrenUpwards`: receives each row with its direct children, bottom-up. Implemented by callers.

members.visit(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.fo: Called for one row after all its descendants. Arguments: the forest, the row id, and its direct children in order (empty for leaves; valid only during the call). Return true to continue, false to stop the walk.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.r.summary: Control object for `Forest.scanDownwards`. Besides the position given by `ForestIterationControl`, it exposes the current row's ancestry and lets the scanner skip parts of the forest. Valid only during the `acceptRow` call.

members.getParent(): Row id of the current row's parent, 0 for a root.
members.getParentIndex(): Index of the current row's parent, -1 for a root.
members.skipSubtree(): Requests that the scan skip the descendants of the current row and continue with the next row after its subtree. Returns that index (which equals `size()` if nothing follows).
members.skipParentSubtree(int): Requests that the scan skip all following rows deeper than `depth`, continuing at the next row whose depth is `depth` or less. With `depth` equal to the current depth this is the same as `skipSubtree`; with a smaller depth it also skips the rest of the ancestor's subtree; -1 ends the scan. Returns the index where the scan will continue. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if `depth` is below -1 or greater than the current depth.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.r.summary: Callback for `Forest.scanDownwards`, receiving rows top-down in forest order. Implemented by callers.

members.acceptRow(com.almworks.jira.structure.ap: Called for each row visited. Arguments: the scan control (position, ancestry, skip and cancel operations) and the row id.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generato.summary: A deferred change produced by a generator's action handler, registered through `HandlingContext.effect(effect, inverse)`. Implemented by generator authors. The plugin calls `apply` while it evaluates a user's edit; `apply` checks feasibility and either blocks or registers the actual work through `EffectContext.effect`. The inverse effect, if given, is kept so the change can be undone later.

members.apply(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.ge: Prepares the change. Should call `context.effect(explanation, runnable)` to register the code that really performs it (run later when the action is carried out), or `context.block`/`context.yield` to refuse. If it neither blocks nor registers anything, the action counts as handled with no work to do. Exceptions thrown here are caught by the plugin, logged, and turn into a block with a generic error message.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generato.summary: Marker base for the objects through which a generator reacts to user edits (add, move, reorder, remove) of rows it produced or controls. Note: the implementation performs no permission checks of its own and does not verify that the module key names an installed generator; callers are responsible for both.

Throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a blank module key; database errors propagate as runtime exceptions.
